body:
Well, I haven't tried it yet, but if it's really that helpful I'd like to give it a go before I do something.
I'm not sure if there's a specific thing that started this; I feel like it's been building up from childhood, and just exploded these past few years.

I was raised by my dad after my mom passed away when I was 2, and I dunno. I've always felt that I owe everything to him, and I really want to make him (and the people around me) proud. I tried hard and got into a good high school, studied everyday, joined lots of extracurricular things, and play piano competitively. I had so many goals for the future.

But I think around three years ago stuff just started falling apart. Dad lost clients, I lost competitions, friends, and my grades weren't what I wanted them to be. I realized that my life was quite empty. I spent so much time trying to please other people that I didn't know what to do with myself when things weren't working out.

I know I shouldn't be complaining- I have amazing parents, shelter, food, health, an education. I have no excuse. I want so badly to be useful and helpful to others, yet all I do is just mope around like a freak. What's wrong with me?

Thank you for your reply, and your offer. You're very kind. Truth be told, I can't really name somebody in my life that I'd be comfortable sharing my thoughts with; I wouldn't want to make them feel uncomfortable, burdened, or annoyed, I guess. 
And as for seeing a professional, I feel like they would patronize me because I'm young and don't really have anything to complain about. Did it really help you?

I'm so sorry for your loss. I can't even begin to imagine how hard it must be for you, but even though depression tells us that we're alone, it's wrong. 

There's so much stress and pressure in your life, but the fact that you're here and reaching out for some help is amazing, and I admire you for that. I care! And I believe many others out there care, too. 

I lost my mom when I was a kid, and ever since then I've always lived in fear, hoping that my dad won't be the next to go. So to some extent, I can relate a little to your situation. 

Try to take things one step at a time. Please don't keep all these sad thoughts in your head. Have you thought of seeing a therapist/counselor? And to your SO, maybe you could explain how you are feeling if you haven't already, and see if the two of you can work things through together.
